newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Interbrew looking at Pripps Ringnes.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Interbrew looking at Pripps Ringnes.

text.p: Belgium's privately owned brewer Interbrew NV, the fourth largest brewing company in the world, said on Monday it was looking at the possible purchase of a stake in Swedish brewery Pripps Ringnes.
"We are still looking at it. As we're still investigating the possibility, we've got no further comment at this stage," Interbrew spokesman Gerard Fauchey said.
A weekend Swedish newspaper report said Interbrew and Dutch brewer Heineken were potential buyers of a 55 percent stake in Pripps held by Swedish automotive group Volvo.

"Pripps Ringnes' strong market position in Sweden and Norway and its successful expansion in the Baltic region and further east makes the company an attractive option for Continental brewery groups," the business daily Dagens Industri said.
Volvo declined to comment on the report, while a Heineken spokeswoman said: "We're always interested in everything, but do not comment on a specific deal until it's closed".
Volvo said in June that it regarded Pripps as a non-core activity which it aimed to sell before the end of the year.
Norwegian food group Orkla owns 45 percent of Pripps. It has an option to buy Volvo's holding in the brewer but is thought to have insufficient financial muscle to do so.
